entities.summary: Giovanni di Cosimo de' Medici was a prominent Italian banker and patron of the arts during the Renaissance. Born around 1429, he inherited the Medici banking dynasty and expanded its operations. He played a significant role in financing several notable artists, including Sandro Botticelli and Leonardo da Vinci. De' Medici's banking empire became a major force in European finance, and his patronage of the arts helped establish Florence as a cultural hub. De' Medici's legacy extended to his descendants, who continued to shape the course of Italian history. The Medici family's influence can still be felt today, with many of their descendants still holding prominent positions in Italian society. De' Medici's life was marked by both great fortune and significant losses, including the loss of his family's wealth during the Wars of the League of Cambrai. Despite these challenges, de' Medici remained a key figure in Florence's cultural and financial landscape until his death in 1463.
